Figure 1:PyRUA-Dex at a glance.Center: our real-world platform playing the piano (a video
frame, cut out), with tactile sensing at the fingertips.(a)Coding agents learn a task’s program in
simulation in two stages, exploration and refinement; the frozen program is deployed in the real world (sim-to-real),
and real-world feedback updates the simulation (real-to-sim; Section3).(b)DexJoCo success
rate with the objects randomized (rand-obj) and with cameras, lighting and textures randomized as well (rand-full;
Section4.5).(c)Tasks learned for the real-world platform: validation layouts completed
in simulation, of 32 (Section5).(d)The nine best of the thirteen four-channel entries on the
Bench2Dex leaderboard, where PyRUA-Dex holds the SOTA (Section4.2).(e)The hands the programs
drive, rendered from their models, with the joints driven per hand (DoF) and whether a program receives tactile
sensing.(f)The tasks of the three settings in five classes, with the number of tasks per setting and one
picture each from simulation and from the real world.

Figure 2:Overview of PyRUA-Dex.All learning takes place in simulation.Stage 1 (exploration):eight
agents (one is drawn) explore the task, each on a training layout of its own with state resets, and share a
memory; their programs are evaluated without the agents and distilled into a task library and one program.Stage 2 (refinement):one agent finds the program’s bottleneck stage by a stage-wise failure analysis,
refines it on randomized layouts and selects the version with the best held-out record. The resulting program
runs frozen, without a language model. For the real world, the simulation is built from the real scene (real-to-sim), the
frozen program is transferred (sim-to-real), and real-world feedback updates the simulation for the next round
of refinement.

Figure 5:Real-to-sim-to-real on our platform.(a)Real-to-sim: what the calibrated simulation
shares with the real robot (cameras, the hands’ drives, fingertip touch, objects and the user’s instructions).(b)Learning in simulation: exploration once, refinement in rounds.(c)Sim-to-real: the frozen
programs on the real robot, behind a safety guard; one pass from (b) to (c) and back is one round.(d)Validation layouts
completed in simulation (of 32) after exploration and after each round of refinement, one chart per task;×\times: the program measured again after the simulation was recalibrated.

Figure 6:Frozen programs on the real robot, head camera unless marked: cube to basket, stacking three cubes,
Night Cruise played with both hands, opening the box by its fabric loop, and writing “Dex” with a brush.
